Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 15:00 - 15:45 PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Laura Chen (CTO, Ironclad Capital), Marcus Reed (Head of Platform), Nina Alvarez (Security Engineer)
Recording: Enabled
summary: Discovery focused on Dedicated capacity needs: Ironclad wants reserved GPUs for latency-sensitive LLM features, strict data isolation, burst capacity for market open spikes, and clear scaling path. Security and compliance (SOC2, KMS, audit logs) are gating factors. Agreed next steps: pricing, benchmarks, SOC2 docs, and scheduling a 1-week pilot for late March.
topics: Performance and KPIs (p99 latency, token throughput)
Security/compliance: SOC2, KMS, SSO, audit logs
transcript:
[00:00] Ava: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Ava from Redwood. Uh, quick round robin?
[00:05] Laura: Hi, this is Laura Chen, CTO at Ironclad Capital.
[00:08] Marcus: Marcus Reed, Head of Platform.
[00:10] Nina: Nina Alvarez, security.
[00:12] Samir: Samir Patel, solutions engineer, Redwood.
[00:15] Ava: Great, goal for today is to understand your latency and isolation requirements and talk about Dedicated capacity options — reserved GPUs, burst, scaling, and anything from security side.
[00:25] Laura: Yep, high level — we have two product features right now: smart summaries for traders and a real-time chat assistant. They both need low p99 latency under 300ms ideally, and, and the chat is most sensitive.
[00:36] Marcus: To add, traffic is a bit spiky — market open and close cause 3-5x spikes for about 10–20 minutes. We want reserved capacity but also a way to burst.
[00:46] Samir: Makes sense. When you say reserved, are you looking at fully isolated Dedicated vs hosted with tenancy?
[00:52] Laura: We prefer Dedicated — data isolation, we need control over network egress, and we have firm compliance needs. Hosted is attractive cost-wise, but security team won't sign off.
[01:05] Nina: Yep, SOC2 and audit logs are musts. We also use AWS KMS for keys and want to keep audit trails.
[01:12] Ava: Understood. Quick question on models — are you using internal fine-tuned models or public open models? That affects KV cache and memory sizing.
[01:20] Marcus: Mostly a tuned variant of an Llama-family model and a smaller embedder. We have the model weights in our S3, we can share sizes.
[01:28] Samir: Ok that helps. For Dedicated, we typically size by peak token throughput and KV cache residency. For your use case with p99 targets, we recommend reserved GPU pool sized for 1.5x your steady peak, plus burst capacity via pre-warmed nodes or shared burst pools — depending on contract.
[01:44] Laura: What's the typical contract language for burst? We need predictable billing but flexibility.
[01:50] Ava: We do reserved capacity with an option for burst credits. You commit to a base pool (monthly), and then you can draw on burst capacity billed at a higher unit rate. We can structure ceiling caps so you don't get surprised.
[02:02] Marcus: And autoscaling? We can't afford slow spin-up during spikes.
[02:06] Samir: We support fast scale-in/out with warm standby kernels — in practice cold starts are 10s of seconds for GPU provisioning; warm buffer nodes are instant. For market spikes we recommend a small warm buffer sized for the expected spike's headroom.
[02:20] Nina: From security, any network requirements? VPC peering? Customer-managed VPC?
[02:25] Ava: For Private deployments we offer full customer-managed VPC and on-prem. For Dedicated we provide a VPC peering option and customer-managed routing — traffic is kept inside your cloud region and we support VPC endpoints, SAML SSO, and KMS integration.
[02:38] Nina: And do you provide audit logs at token level? We need request/response logs and redaction options.
[02:44] Samir: Yes, we emit structured logs — request id, model, token counts, latency. Full request/response logging can be enabled with redaction. We also support pushing logs to your SIEM via CloudWatch or GCS.
[02:58] Marcus: Great. Can you speak to model variants and fallback? If our primary GPU pool hits capacity, how do you handle traffic?
[03:05] Samir: Smart routing. We can fallback to a compatible smaller model or routed to hosted pool as fallback depending on policy. For Dedicated customers we typically set a policy for best-effort local fallbacks and then offer cross-region or hosted fallback as last resort.
[03:18] Laura: We need deterministic behavior for SLAs — if fallback happens, we need to be notified and have a circuit-breaker.
[03:24] Ava: Absolutely, we can surface events in the console and push alerts. Also we can attach runbooks and automated rollback policies for model rollouts.
[03:34] Marcus: Can you give an example pricing sketch? rough order of magnitude per GPU?
[03:38] Ava: Ballpark — depends on GPU class and commitment. For A100-80GB equivalent a committed monthly pool might be in the low tens of thousands per GPU per month with discounts for annual. Burst usage billed at a premium. We'll send exact SKUs.
[03:52] Laura: Sounds good. We'll need numbers to run TCO.
[03:55] Nina: A couple security specifics: key management — can Redwood integrate with our AWS KMS or do you require passing keys?
[04:02] Samir: We integrate with customer-managed KMS; keys never leave your control for encrypting customer data at rest. For any managed secrets we support HSM integration on request.
[04:12] Nina: And certification evidence — can you share SOC2 Type II and penetration test summary?
[04:17] Ava: Yes, we'll include SOC2 and pen-test summary in the doc bundle.
[04:22] Marcus: For performance — do you have benchmarks for p99 latency at different sequence lengths and batching? This will impact our prompt design.
[04:30] Samir: We track latency profiles and kernel selection per model family; we'll share a benchmark template and recommended batch settings. For chat we usually recommend small batch sizes and KV caching to keep p99 low. For summaries you can batch more aggressively.
[04:44] Laura: On caching — is prefix/KV cache sticky to GPUs or shared? We worry about cache warm-up and cold misses.
[04:51] Samir: Good Q — KV cache is managed by the runtime and can be local to instances. For Dedicated you can allocate larger KV cache residency to reduce cold misses. We also offer warm cache pre-warming strategies during scheduled events (market open).
[05:03] Marcus: What about multi-tenant noise? We need isolation so noisy neighbors don't affect us.
[05:08] Ava: Dedicated pools are tenant-isolated; you get reserved instances and CPU/GPU affinity. We can also offer network segmentation and IOPS guarantees for storage.
[05:18] Nina: Any data residency controls? We must keep data in us-east-1 for regulatory reasons.
[05:23] Samir: Yes, you can pin deployments to regions and we support on-prem if necessary. For Dedicated we deploy in the chosen region only.
[05:31] Laura: Ok timeline question — if we sign a pilot, how quickly can you provision a Dedicated pool for a 1-week pilot?
[05:37] Ava: For a pilot we can provision within 1–2 weeks depending on contractual sign-off and networking setup — if you want a quick start we can do a hosted-backed pilot in days while we stand up Dedicated nodes.
[05:49] Marcus: We'll prefer a Dedicated-backed pilot to validate infra. Can you support a 1-week window late March?
[05:55] Ava: Yes, that should be doable — we'll confirm in follow-ups.
[05:58] Nina: One more: encryption in transit — do you support mTLS between your control plane and customer VPC?
[06:03] Samir: We support TLS and mTLS for customer-managed endpoints and peering.
[06:08] Laura: Are there limitations on model uploads? size limits, transfer times?
[06:12] Samir: No hard limits but large model transfer may take time; we recommend sharing weights through our secure transfer or S3 presigned links. We can assist with ingestion.
[06:21] Marcus: Let's talk about scaling policy details — we want predictable autoscaling thresholds based on queued requests or token backlog.
[06:28] Samir: Our autoscaler can be configured by queue depth, average token throughput, or latency SLOs. For latency sensitive workloads use latency-based policy with warm buffer nodes to avoid cold starts.
[06:38] Laura: What's the observability? We need token-level cost breakdowns for chargebacks.
[06:43] Ava: Redwood Console provides per-route and per-model cost breakdowns, token counts, latencies, traces, and per-token cost estimates. You can also export to BI tools.
[06:54] Marcus: Any known gotchas?
[06:56] Samir: Watch out for KV cache churn if you have highly distinct conversation contexts; that affects memory sizing. Also quantization can change latency/quality tradeoffs — we can advise per workload.
[07:08] Laura: On quality — do you support A/B rollouts between model quantization profiles?
[07:12] Samir: Yes, rollouts with canary and automatic rollback if quality regresses. We integrate eval hooks to detect regressions against your prompt sets.
[07:21] Nina: For compliance, what about data deletion and retention policies?
[07:25] Ava: You can set retention policies per route and have on-demand deletion; we'll include docs.
[07:30] Laura: Good. Let's recap next steps.
[07:33] Ava: Sure — I will send Dedicated pricing, contract template, and the SOC2/pen test docs. Samir will share benchmark spreadsheet and test harness guidance. Marcus will share traffic profiles and expected peak QPS. Nina will send compliance question list. We will aim to provision pilot late March.
[07:50] Marcus: Sounds good.
[07:51] Nina: Thanks all.
[07:52] Ava: Thanks, we'll follow up with the artifacts and proposed dates.
[07:56] [call ends]
